$comment: Tenant-data entry points that do NOT reference the tenant lifecycle vocabulary. Each needs a justification saying why the surface does not need an entitlement check. This list may only SHRINK: wire the check, then re-run with --write-baseline. Adding an entry by hand is a regression, not a fix.

server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts.reason: DELIBERATELY UNCONDITIONAL. Verifies every tamper-evident audit store estate-wide (audit_logs chain and seals, audit_events linkage and seals, audit.tamper_proof_log, the immutability triggers) under a system scope. The only organization_id it reads is the grouping column of the audit_events chain, which is per organisation by construction; it is never a tenant filter. Audit integrity is precisely the thing that must NOT stop when a tenant is suspended, pending deletion or purged - 21 CFR Part 11 11.10(e) expects the trail to outlive the records it describes. Gating this on entitlement would blind the platform to chain damage in exactly the tenants under scrutiny. Re-read 2026-09-25 after the sweep grew from one store to six (security audit 2026-09-24 DP-06/DP-04, P0-9a/P0-8a, commit e8724680). Re-read 2026-10-01 after the sweep began anchoring the audit_logs chain head outside the database (P0-8 anchor, DP-04; fix round DP-68): through server/services/audit/chain-anchor.ts it now reads every organisation's chain head (tenant_id, head row id, chain_seq, sha256_chain, row count, time) in one statement, verifies it against the latest anchor, and writes the next anchor to the object-locked evidence bucket (AUDIT_ANCHOR_BUCKET). Still under the system scope, still refusing a tenant-scoped connection, and still DELIBERATELY UNCONDITIONAL: a suspended, pending-deletion or purged tenant's chain head is exactly the one whose truncation must be detected. What leaves the database is identifiers, hashes, counts and times, never row content; tenant_id is the chain's grouping key, never a tenant filter. RE-READ 2026-10-01: 4b1583a2c (U19) wrapped the call in runScheduledOncePerWindow so one check runs per day across processes; scope and stores unchanged. The justification holds. Re-read 2026-10-01 (P0-8 follow-ups): every run now also reports the latest anchor's age, from the anchor's own anchoredAt and the sweep's clock, and raises a `stale` incident through the same alert path when it is older than 48 hours; a stale anchor does not block the next anchor. Nothing new is read from any tenant, nothing new is written, scope and stores are unchanged. The justification holds. RE-READ 2026-10-15 against 2f28ce51d (the seal check reports `unverifiable` instead of `ok` over zero verified seals, and names rows unsealed after sealing began): only the verdict over the same walk changed. Nothing new is read from any tenant, nothing new is written, the scope is still the system scope and the stores are unchanged. The justification holds.

server/jobs/retentionCron.ts.reason: DELIBERATELY UNCONDITIONAL. Retention deletion must run FOR non-entitled tenants — that is its purpose. A suspended or pending-deletion tenant is the primary case, and gating it on entitlement would mean data is never retained out of the tenants whose retention clock is actually running. Its only notification path (notifyAdmins) addresses PLATFORM admins with an estate summary, not tenant users. RE-READ 2026-09-10 against d32dc3c5f ("Stop the retention sweep destroying records under legal hold"), which is what drifted this digest. The justification is unchanged by it: a legal hold is a per-record protection applied across the whole estate, not a tenant-entitlement gate, and the sweep still runs for non-entitled tenants. Two properties worth carrying forward — loadActiveHolds reads vaultLegalHolds estate-wide and unscoped, which is correct for a platform sweep and must not be 'fixed' into a tenant-scoped read; and it FAILS CLOSED, so an unreadable hold table aborts the sweep having deleted nothing. No tenant-facing notification path was added; notifyAdmins still addresses RETENTION_ADMIN_EMAILS, i.e. platform operators. RE-READ 2026-09-26 against the P1-22 rewrite (the disposition of one document is one transaction with its chained audit row; the sweep is scheduled at boot behind ENABLE_RETENTION_SWEEP; retention_until is set at admission): unchanged — still estate-wide under the system scope, holds still read unscoped and failing closed, notification still to platform administrators. RE-READ 2026-09-29 against VR-07 (docs/evidence/D5/2026-09-29-vault-record-no-delete/), which drifted this digest: a policy that asks for destruction now leaves the record untouched and is counted as destructionRefused, because the database refuses to delete a recorded version. Unchanged otherwise: still estate-wide under the system scope, holds still read unscoped and failing closed, and the refusal is reported only to platform administrators (notifyAdmins and the log). No entitlement gate and no tenant-facing path. RE-READ 2026-10-01: 4b1583a2c (U19) and 177a0a00f moved the admin summary onto services/emailService.ts; recipients are still RETENTION_ADMIN_EMAILS (platform admins), not tenant users, and no entitlement gate was added. The justification holds; only this digest was refreshed.
